_comment: Master config for caero_rings. Edit values here, run ./scripts/apply-config.sh, then build+deploy.

ore_bias._comment: Default count multiplier per tier. 1.0 = vanilla. Per-ore overrides below. Ore 'family' matches the placed_feature prefix (e.g., 'diamond' covers ore_diamond, ore_diamond_medium, ore_diamond_buried; 'zinc' covers create's zinc_ore).

biome_ore_overrides._comment: Per-biome ore multipliers vs VANILLA. Every biome listed gets its own pair of biome modifiers (id_remove_features for the tier-scaled & vanilla variants, add_features for the biome-specific variant). EVERY family must be specified, every value must be in [0.2, 2.0], and the 8 multipliers must average to the tier midpoint (easy 0.7, medium 1.0, hard 1.5). The 2.0× cap keeps us safely under Minecraft's count-placement maximum of 256 (highest vanilla count is ore_iron_upper=90, so 90×2.0=180). apply-config.py asserts all three constraints.

minecraft:badlands._note: HARD. Canon: badlands are gold country. Copper-poor surface.

minecraft:eroded_badlands._note: HARD. Like badlands but rarer — push gold + redstone harder.

minecraft:wooded_badlands._note: MEDIUM. Easier-to-reach badlands variant, milder gold bonus.

minecraft:snowy_slopes._note: HARD. Approach to peaks — iron + diamond + lapis.

minecraft:ice_spikes._note: HARD. Rare — diamond + lapis + redstone, low warm metals.

minecraft:swamp._note: MEDIUM. Decay biome — coal-rich, iron poor.

minecraft:desert._note: MEDIUM. Sun-baked sandstone. Copper + lapis bias.

minecraft:windswept_hills._note: MEDIUM. Iron mountains, cold and bare.

minecraft:windswept_forest._note: MEDIUM. Forested mountain — softer iron lean.

minecraft:mushroom_fields._note: EASY. Alien — heavy redstone, low everything else. Rare island; reward the trip.

minecraft:cherry_grove._note: EASY. Pretty rare biome — lapis+gold festive palette.

regions_unexplored:fungal_fen._note: MEDIUM. Wet weird biome — redstone/zinc theme.

ore_list._comment: Overworld ore placed_features that get rescaled across every biome in a tier. Only include features that get spawned in (effectively) every overworld biome — features that vanilla restricts to specific biomes (copper_large in dripstone caves, gold_extra in badlands, emerald in mountains/meadow) get added to every tier biome here, which causes 3-8× over-supply. Move those to remove_only instead. Strings default to namespace=minecraft. Use {namespace, name} for modded ores (e.g. Create's zinc_ore).
ore_list._remove_only_comment: Stripped from every tier so they don't stack on the scaled replacements, but no scaled replacement is added. Two reasons a feature lands here: (a) it uses a placement format the count-scaling generator can't rescale (rarity_filter, uniform-count), or (b) it's biome-restricted in vanilla and spraying it across all tier biomes would over-supply the tier.

bic_spawn_boost._comment: ADDITIVE multiplier on top of BiC's default 1x neoforge:any spawns. medium=0.5 means +0.5x = 1.5x total. Values apply to weight, not count.

tier_spawn_handler._comment: Runtime directed BiC spawning near players (TierSpawnHandler.kt). NOT auto-synced from this config yet — edit the Kotlin file directly.

chest_mass._comment: Extra physics mass added per item in any container BE on a Create Aeronautics contraption. Per-item bonus = mass_per_weight_unit × stack.count × Encumbered weight. Sable's baseline solid-block mass is 1.0, so 0.02 ≈ 2% of a real block per item. max_bonus_per_block caps a single container; set to 0 (or any non-positive value) for fully linear scaling — no cap.

water_discount._comment: When a contraption is sitting on water, scale its chest+player mass bonuses by (1 - discount). 0.7 = boats only feel 30% of the cargo penalty airships do, biasing players toward water transport for heavy loads. Detection is binary: 1 fluid lookup per physics tick at the bottom of the contraption's pose. Set enabled=false to disable.

horse_encumbrance._comment: Slow horses/donkeys/mules/camels in proportion to the rider's Encumbered inventory weight. limit = limit_multiplier × Encumbered.threshold2 (so the horse can carry 2× a player's normal limit). speed_after_slow = base × (1 - ratio × max_slow), where ratio = clamp(weight/limit, 0, 1). For the heavy-load zone to actually be reachable, set Encumbered's horse/donkey/mule/camel thresholds to 0 in config/encumbered-server.toml — otherwise Encumbered auto-dismounts at threshold2 and the slow only applies up to 50% of the curve.

player_mass._comment: Players standing on a Create Aeronautics contraption add their carried inventory weight to the contraption's physics mass. bonus_per_player = base_mass + Encumbered.calculateWeight(player) × inventory_multiplier. Applied via a mixin on MergedMassTracker.uploadData — every physics tick re-reads who's tracking the contraption and adds their weight; walking off stops the contribution immediately on the next tick (no state to clean up). max_per_player caps a single player's contribution; 0 = no cap.
